transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Um… I guess what brings me in is that I’m having a really hard time staying seated when I’m supposed to. Like, not just being a little restless, but actually getting up at the wrong times.

It’s been happening during client interviews, which is embarrassing because in my line of work I’m supposed to be observing and listening carefully, not popping up to look out the window or grab something or just… move. And it’s not only work. I tutor sometimes, and even there I’ll find myself standing up when I should be sitting with someone and paying attention. Even at book club, where the whole point is to sit and talk and listen, I keep getting up. People have started noticing, and I can tell it comes across like I’m not interested or I’m impatient, but it’s more like I just can’t stay put. That’s the main thing that made me think, okay, maybe I should talk to someone about this.

You mentioned having trouble staying seated at work, tutoring, and in book club. Does this also happen in other situations, like at home when you're trying to relax or during meetings outside of work?

Yes, I mean… the main places I really notice it are the ones where I’m clearly expected to stay seated and be attentive. Client interviews are the biggest one because it’s so obvious and, honestly, kind of mortifying. I’ll be sitting there trying to listen, and then I’m suddenly up—getting water, checking something by the window, adjusting something that doesn’t really need adjusting. It’s like my body decides before I’ve really thought it through.

And tutoring is similar, because I’m supposed to be right there with the person, focused on them, and I’ll stand up in the middle of it like I need to move around the room. Book club too, which sounds minor, but people are literally just sitting and discussing a book, and I’m the one who keeps getting up. It’s not that I’m bored or trying to be rude. I actually want to listen. I just have this very hard time staying put, and people are starting to notice.
Can you tell me if, besides having trouble staying seated, you also find yourself easily distracted, having difficulty focusing on tasks, or acting without thinking things through?

Um… I’m not completely sure how to answer that, because the thing I can really point to clearly is the not staying seated part. That’s the one that feels obvious and measurable, like people can see it happening.

As far as being easily distracted or having trouble focusing, I don’t know… I mean, I suppose everyone has moments where their mind wanders, but I haven’t really been tracking that the same way. And “acting without thinking things through” — I’m not sure. I don’t want to say yes just because it sounds like it might fit. The main thing I’ve noticed is that I get up before I’ve really decided to, if that makes sense. Like my body moves first. But beyond that, I’d probably need you to explain what kinds of examples you mean, because I don’t want to overstate it.

Can you think of times when you've had real trouble keeping your focus on what you're doing — like starting tasks but not finishing them, getting easily pulled away by things around you, or someone speaking to you and not really hearing them? And if so, how often does that happen?

I’m honestly not sure I can give you a clean yes to that. I can think of ordinary moments where, you know, I’m reading something and I have to reread a paragraph, or someone says something and I need them to repeat it, but I don’t know that I’ve noticed it as a real pattern the way I’ve noticed the getting-up thing.

The starting-tasks-and-not-finishing part… I mean, I’d have to think about that more carefully. I don’t want to sit here and accidentally make it sound bigger than it is just because you asked it that way. Same with being pulled away by things around me. In my work, there are always details to notice, so sometimes shifting attention is kind of part of the job, if that makes sense. But whether I’m unusually distractible? I don’t know.

The thing I can say clearly is that when I’m supposed to stay seated and engaged, my body kind of acts before I’ve fully decided to move. But in terms of focus problems specifically, I haven’t really been keeping track, so I’d be guessing a bit.

Have you found yourself doing things without fully thinking about them first — like interrupting others, making quick decisions without considering the consequences, or blurting things out — even if it's not something you intended to do?

Yes… that one I can recognize more than the focus thing, I think. Not so much, like, making huge reckless decisions, at least not that I can think of off the top of my head, but interrupting or inserting myself—yes.

At work, especially with the junior detectives, if I overhear them talking through a lead or trying to figure out what to do next, I’ll just jump in. I’ll ask questions, or I’ll start giving advice, and sometimes it’s useful, but the problem is I wasn’t actually asked. I’ll realize afterward, “Oh, I just barged into their conversation.” It’s almost like I hear the thread of something and my brain goes, “Wait, I know something about that,” and then my mouth is already moving before I’ve checked whether it’s appropriate.

It happens outside work too, which is embarrassing. Like if a neighbor is talking in the hallway about something, I might step in with a suggestion or a question before I’ve really been invited into the conversation. And then a minute later I feel awkward because I can tell I may have overstepped. I don’t mean to be pushy or intrusive. In the moment it feels like I’m just being helpful or curious, but afterward I can see that I sort of inserted myself where I didn’t belong.
Do you often find yourself fidgeting, tapping your hands or feet, or squirming in your seat when you're trying to stay still, even if you're not getting up entirely?

Yes. That one I do notice, especially when I’m forced to sit at the computer for long stretches. A lot of my work can be sitting there combing through records, cross-checking names, dates, addresses, that kind of thing, and I’ll realize my foot has been bouncing under the desk the entire time. Or I’ll be clicking a pen without really meaning to. Sometimes I’m shifting around in the chair so much that I have to stop and find my place again in what I was reading.

It’s not always that I actually get up and leave the desk — though sometimes that’s the urge — but even when I’m technically still sitting there, I’m not exactly still. It’s like some part of me has to keep moving. And it’s annoying, honestly, because the work requires careful attention to detail, and if I’m squirming around or fidgeting too much, I can lose the thread and have to go back over the same section again.

Can you think of specific times when you started a task but had real trouble finishing it — not just because it was boring or you got interrupted, but because your attention shifted and you couldn’t get back to it? And if so, how often would you say that happens?

I’m still not sure I can give you a solid example of that, honestly. I’m trying to think of one where I started something, my attention shifted, and then I just couldn’t get back to it, and nothing specific is jumping out at me in a way that feels fair to say.

I mean, there are plenty of tasks that take me longer than I think they should, especially if there are a lot of pieces to keep track of. But I can usually point to some reason — a phone call, another lead coming in, needing to verify something, realizing there’s a missing document, that sort of thing. In my line of work, tasks don’t always have a neat beginning and end, so it’s hard for me to separate “I didn’t finish because my attention wandered” from “the task got complicated or got paused for a legitimate reason.”

If you mean something like I’m halfway through a report and then I drift off into something else and never come back to it… I don’t know. I’m not saying it never happens, because I’m sure there are ordinary moments like that, but I haven’t noticed it as a recurring problem I could put a frequency on. I’d be guessing if I said daily or weekly or anything like that.
Can you think of times when you started something but had real trouble finishing it because your mind was no longer on the task, even if there wasn’t an outside interruption?

I’m still drawing a bit of a blank on that specific version of it. I’m not trying to be difficult — I just don’t want to invent an example because I know what you’re asking for sounds pretty specific.

If I start something and don’t finish it, I can usually explain it some other way. Like the task changes, or I need information from someone else, or something else becomes more urgent. With investigative work, that happens constantly, so it’s hard to say, “No, this was purely because my mind left the task.” I’m sure there are moments where I look up and realize I’ve drifted, or I have to reread something because I wasn’t really absorbing it, but that’s a little different from starting a task and then being unable to finish it because my attention moved on.

So… I guess my honest answer is I haven’t noticed that as a clear pattern. It may happen in small ways, but I can’t point to a repeated situation where there was no outside interruption and I just couldn’t get myself back to the thing.
